commands.summary: Found the Desktop shortcut's TargetPath was 'C:\Users\jerem\AppData\Local\Packages\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc\LocalCache\Local\RepoPact Workbench\repopact-desktop.exe' -- a path that only resolves inside Claude Code's own sandboxed/virtualized filesystem view, not Jeremy's real Desktop or AppData. Confirmed by diffing the two paths' contents (identical file, size, timestamp), proving Windows was transparently redirecting AppData/Desktop path resolution for the NSIS installer process because it was launched from my sandboxed tool session. Every prior 'verified' check of this shortcut (including in 20260911-062-windows-nsis-and-android-icon.json) was unknowingly checking that same redirected view and reported false positives. The Start-menu shortcut happened to resolve correctly (Tauri's own template creates it differently than my custom NSIS hook's $DESKTOP usage), so only the Desktop shortcut was actually broken for Jeremy.

environment.lesson: Any Windows install/shortcut-creation step performed through this agent's own sandboxed process is unreliable for AppData/Desktop-class paths due to Windows filesystem virtualization for containerized apps; such steps must be run directly by the operator (or verified by the operator) rather than trusted from agent-side checks alone.
